about: Saved Claude results from the Prompt lab, shown on the demo site. Built from prompt-lab-log.json by scripts/build-demo-results.mjs (newest run per product and element). Each `reply` has the same shape as the AI's reply, so live AI can replace this file later.

inputs.what: How expense approvals work for managers
inputs.next: Apporvals go to the right person immediately

options.why: Pick this for most screens where managers need the point fast on a phone.

parts.label: Body
parts.text: When an employee submits an expense, it goes to the right approver immediately. You review it and decide.

options.why: Pick this for first-time setup or onboarding, where managers want confidence in the process.

parts.label: Body
parts.text: You don't need to chase anything. Each expense goes to the right person as soon as it's submitted.

options.why: Pick this for tight mobile spaces like banners, empty states or tooltips.

parts.label: Body
parts.text: Approvals go to the right person immediately.

left_out: How 'the right person' is decided (for example, by team, amount or manager). Not provided, so the copy doesn't say.
What approvers can do beyond reviewing and deciding (for example, reject, comment or request changes). Not provided.
Whether approvers are notified, and how. Not provided, so no notification is promised.

inputs.next: An email is sent to the employee who asked for the approval

options.why: Pick this for the main approval action on most screens, where speed matters.
Pick this on small mobile screens or lists where space is tight.
Pick this when a final step needs to make the commitment explicit.

left_out: Did not mention what happens after approval (payment, notifications, reimbursement timing) because none of it was listed.
Did not state whether approval can be undone, since that behavior was not provided.

inputs.what: A new account has no invoices yet

options.why: Pick this for most screens where you want a clear, fast path to the first invoice.

parts.label: Body
parts.text: Create your first invoice to get started.

options.why: Pick this when new accounts may wonder whether something is missing or broken.

parts.label: Body
parts.text: This is normal for a new account, so create your first invoice when you're ready.

options.why: Pick this for small mobile screens where space is tight and the action is obvious.

parts.label: Body
parts.text: Create an invoice and it will appear here.

left_out: Did not mention what happens after an invoice is created (such as approval steps, notifications, or where it is stored), since those behaviors weren't provided.
Did not mention required fields, invoice import options, or how long setup takes, as none were given.
The Concise option says the invoice will appear on this screen; confirm that matches product behavior.

inputs.what: The card payment for a subscription failed at checkout
inputs.next: Try again or use another card

options.why: Pick this for most screens where you want to state the problem and next step plainly.

parts.label: Body
parts.text: Your card payment failed at checkout. Try again or use another card.

options.why: Pick this when the reader may worry about their payment or card.

parts.label: Body
parts.text: The card payment didn't go through at checkout. You can try again or choose a different card.

options.why: Pick this for small mobile screens, banners or toasts where space is tight.

parts.label: Body
parts.text: Try again, or use another card.

left_out: The reason the card payment failed (for example declined, expired or network issue), since it wasn't provided.
Whether the reader was charged or whether their cart or details were saved, since no facts were given.
Any support contact or help link, since none was provided.

inputs.what: This is a headline for when a startup founder wants to add their company
inputs.next: It only takes a second to add a company and it's free

options.why: Pick this for most screens: it states the action plainly for busy founders.
Pick this when you want to stress speed and cost right at the top.

parts.label: Headline
parts.text: Add your company in seconds, free

options.why: Pick this for a warmer first-time moment, like onboarding or an empty state.

left_out: Did not say what happens after the company is added (for example, applying to accelerators or grants), since no product behavior was listed.
Used 'seconds' for 'only takes a second'; confirm the exact time claim before shipping.

inputs.next: Adding spaces or leaving out the country code

options.why: Pick this for most screens: it states the format rule plainly in one line.

parts.label: Text
parts.text: Start with the two-letter country code, like DE or GB.

options.why: Pick this when seeing a real format helps more than reading a rule.

parts.label: Text
parts.text: Include the country code at the start, for example GB29NWBK60161331926819.

options.why: Pick this when spaces are the main mistake and you want to ease worry.

parts.label: Text
parts.text: Enter the full IBAN, starting with the country code. Spaces are fine.

left_out: I don't know whether the field accepts or strips spaces, so the Direct and Example-led options don't mention them.
The Reassuring option says spaces are fine, which only works if the product accepts them. Confirm this before choosing it, or drop that sentence.
The example IBAN is a format illustration only. Confirm it is acceptable to show, or swap in your own placeholder.

options.why: Pick this for most screens: it states the result plainly and fits a quick approval flow.
Pick this when you want to signal the action is complete and no further step is needed.
Pick this for batch approvals on small phone screens where space and attention are tight.

inputs.what: This is a tooltip explaining that the information written in the field won't be disclosed publicly
inputs.next: Try again or use another card

parts.label: Text
parts.text: This information won't be shown publicly.

options.why: Pick this for sensitive fields where founders may hesitate to share details.

parts.label: Text
parts.text: You can enter this with confidence, because it won't be made public.

options.why: Pick this when space is tight, such as small fields or mobile layouts.

left_out: Who can see this information (for example, accelerators or grant providers reviewing your application), since that wasn't provided.
How the information is stored or used, since that wasn't provided.
The field label, so the copy avoids repeating it. Naming the field could make the tooltip more specific.
